label: Second copy-phase step: outputting original token 1 right after <DEL>
explanation: Positional feature for the start of the copy phase. It fires on the step right after <DEL> is input (recall_idx == 1, input = original token 0 fed back, output = original token 1). That is 89% of such steps and 91% of activation mass. It also has a weak tail at recall_idx == 2 (about 0.1-0.3 of max, ~8% of mass), mostly for longer sequences. Magnitude rises with sequence length: near zero for L=3-4, and all top activations (~5.3) come from L=8-9 at recall_idx 1. It does not depend on token identity (in_tok, out_tok and first_tok lifts are all flat). It is essentially silent in the original phase, on the <DEL> step itself, and at recall_idx >= 3.

issues: Length dependence at recall_idx 1 is a hard step, not just 'magnitude rises with length'. On dev, recall_idx==1 has precision 0.0 at L=3 (0 of 13065 steps active), 0.395 at L=4, and 1.0 at every L from 5 to 9. The explanation mentions the L=4 weakness but leaves out that L=3 is completely silent. The label ('outputting original token 1 right after <DEL>') does not say that short sequences are excluded.

The recall_idx 2 tail is partial even where the predicate includes it. Precision of recall_idx==2 is 0.71 at L=7, 0.75 at L=8 and 0.62 at L=9. It is also 0.43 at L=6, which the predicate leaves out (about 1% of mass, the main class of missed activations in the test misses output). Which recall_idx 2 steps fire is not explained by anything I tested: digit vs letter input, n_digits and correct all leave precision flat (0.66-0.76). This looks like a threshold effect on a weak tail, not a missed variable.
The same goes for L=4 at recall_idx 1: digit vs letter input and n_digits do not separate active from inactive steps (precision 0.32-0.42 in every case).
Small off-target activity: about 5% of the last original-token steps fire at L=9 (orig_idx 8, about 0.1% of mass), and recall_idx 8 fires about 0.2% of the time. Both are negligible.

The other claims check out on dev. Activation mass is 0.999 in the copy phase; recall_idx 1 is active 88.6% of the time with 91.5% of mass; recall_idx 2 holds 8.4% of mass; the <DEL> step and recall_idx >= 3 are essentially silent; in_tok and out_tok lifts are flat. The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.823, R 0.935, F1 0.875, mass recall 0.988.
